name: Anova Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in anova work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.
content:
This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in anova work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Check that anova terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
2. Measure before optimizing any anova bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
3. When anova guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
4. Keep anova changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
5. Prefer the simplest anova approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
6. Re-check edge cases relevant to anova (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
7. Prefer explicit, readable anova solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
8. State assumptions about anova explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
9. Surface known limitations of a chosen anova approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
10. Validate anova outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of anova correctness.
- Do not skip documenting anova assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not apply generic anova advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid mixing unrelated anova concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for anova, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
